the synthesis, structure determination, and properties of a novel complex, MoO(S3 CPh)(η3 -S2CPh), which was obtained by the oxidation of MoO(S3 CNp) (η3 -S 2CNp), where Np is naphthyl, with 2,3-dichloro-5,6-dicyano-1,4-benzoquinone.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this complex is the first example of a trithioperoxide ligand coordinated to a transition metal ion.

the complex MoO(S3 CPh)(η3 S2CPh) is the first example of an oxomolybdate complex containing both η3 -dihydroxydithiolate (η3 S2) and trithioperoxide ligands, and the first example of a molybdenum complex containing both η2 -dithiolate and η3 -trithioperoxido ligands.
the complex MoO(S3Ph)(η3 -S2Ph) has been synthesized and characterized by elemental analysis, infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray crystallography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reaction between the dithiobenzoyl anion (S2CPh) and oxomolybdate(V) in an acidic aqueenous medium leads to the formation of a novel oxomolybdo complex containing a trithioperoxobenzoato (S2COPhO) ligand.
the complex MoO(S3 CPh)(η3 -S2 CPh) is the first oxomolybdate(V) complex with a trithioperoxobenzoato group coordinated to the metal center.
the reaction between molybdate and dithiobenzates in acidic aqueous media is an excellent way to synthesize novel molybdenum complexes with dithiobezoate or trithioperoxobezoate ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction of the sodium molybdates with diethylamino dithiobenzates leads to the synthesis of the novel oxomolybdo complexes.
the reaction of MoO2+4 with S2CPh2- leads to a complex with two ligand molecules, S2CPh- and O3SCPh-, which are bound to the metal ion in an unusual manner.
a trithioperoxide group can act as a bridging group between two molybdenum centers.
